summaries.demographer: Catherine Denis is a 62-year-old never-married woman living alone in a rented house in Dallas, Texas, with no children or cohabiting partner (Q51, Q84). She is a first-generation Honduran American, born in Dallas to Honduran immigrant parents, bilingual in Spanish and English, and identifies as Hispanic/Latina and mestiza (Q86-Q89). She has a bachelor's degree in food science and nutrition and works full time as a salaried food service operations manager (Q90, Q65). Her life-course profile shows stable employment, strong kin ties outside the household, and aging-related planning around retirement, health, and housing security (Q05, Q83, Q108).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Catherine is strongly routine-driven, risk-averse, and future-oriented, with budgeting, savings, and emergency planning serving as core behavioral anchors (Q57, Q61, Q82). She prefers predictable systems and debt avoidance, choosing modest travel and controlled spending over consumption that would weaken savings (Q62, Q63). Her work behavior reflects high responsibility and loss aversion around operational errors, especially food safety and staffing failures (Q65, Q78). She responds to uncertainty by making lists, delegating cautiously, and preserving buffers of time, money, and procedure (Q18, Q43).
summaries.political_scientist: Catherine is a consistent voter and identifies as a moderate Democrat, closer to the Democratic Party than the Republican Party (Q23, Q95, Q96). Her civic orientation is practical and institutionally minded: she values health care access, workers, immigration fairness, public services, and competent administration (Q24). She is sympathetic to Black Lives Matter concerns and thinks about racism and policing through accountability, dignity, and institutional correction rather than protest-centered activism (Q26-Q30). Her community engagement is rooted in church, food distribution, voter awareness, and local service rather than partisan performance (Q17, Q29, Q47).
summaries.psychologist: Catherine presents as conscientious, disciplined, orderly, and responsibility-focused, with a strong identity as the person who keeps systems and people steady (Q01, Q65, Q109). She manages stress through routine, walking, prayer, tea, knitting, music, baking, and written lists, while recognizing work-related anxiety and a tendency to overfunction (Q43-Q45, Q50). Her relational style is loyal but selective: she prefers small, dependable circles and low-drama relationships (Q05-Q07). Current psychological tension centers on retirement, delegation, and separating self-worth from being indispensable at work (Q18, Q44, Q108).
